newsitem.title: USA: Estee Lauder executive sued for harassment.
newsitem.headline: Estee Lauder executive sued for harassment.

text.p: A woman employee of Estee Lauder has sued a top male executive for $1 million alleging that she was forced to take a lower paying job in another division to avoid his unwanted sexual advances.
In the sexual harassment lawsuit filed in Mahattan Supreme Court on Tuesday, Barbara Gretzen accused Robert Nielsen, president of the firm's Aramis men's division, of "predatory sexual behaviour".
A spokeswoman for Estee Lauder said, "the case has no merit" and the company will "contest it vigorously."

According to the lawsuit, Gretzen joined Aramis in 1994 as Nielsen's executive assistant on an annual salary of $50,000. She alleged that the harassment began in March 1995 when Nielsen told her he had had an erotic dream about her. Gretzen alleged that Nielsen told her he was having "sexual thoughts" about her constantly.

Nielsen had held out the possibility of a promotion to marketing, according to Gretzen, but Nielsen never mentioned the job again after she told him he was making her uncomfortable with his unwanted advances.
She alleged that Nielsen later cost her a bigger promotion to executive assistant for Estee lauder chairman Leonard Lauder.
